summary.text: 白 means “white.” Its early graph is treated as one picture, but its subject is disputed: proposals include a thumb and a cooking or measuring vessel.

formation.text: Pictographic: the early graph is treated as one picture. A thumb is one proposed subject; another proposal identifies a cooking or measuring vessel, with the middle stroke marking the join between lid and body. Neither identification is settled.

components.text: The early graph is one pictorial form, not a combination of separate parts. Its referent is disputed: proposals include a thumb and a cooking or measuring vessel.

history.text: The graph is reported to develop from oracle-bone forms through bronze and small-seal forms to regular script. The early referent remains disputed; this proposed sequence does not identify the picture’s subject.
The Shuowen tradition explains the seal form as 入 joined with 二, interpreting 二 as an “yin number.” This is a historical explanation of the graph, not confirmation of its early pictorial origin.

uncertainties.text: Other proposed subjects include cloth, flame or light, and a face or head. The vessel proposal does not establish the object's ancient name or pronunciation.

Early uses for the color word 白, 伯, and a place name are reported, but their order and first-attestation dates are unresolved. A thumb-based account connects 伯 with the thumb's proposed leading position; another proposes borrowing based on sound, without establishing the sound match. The reported use for “hundred” has no secure semantic link to “white.”
Comparative proposals for the spoken word 白 differ, and neither identifies a sound-bearing component in the graph.

limitations.text: The order of early uses and their exact first-attestation dates are unresolved. The proposed sound-based borrowing involving 伯 establishes neither a direction nor a confirmed sound match; the proposed depicted object's name and pronunciation are also unknown.
The reported use for “hundred” does not establish a semantic transition from “white.”

“Pure, unblemished” and “bright” are current dictionary-listed senses. One proposed account links white with purity, then brightness with daylight, and continues through clarity to reporting. The steps are undated, so this sequence remains unestablished.

takeaway.text: Early uses include 白 for “white” and 伯. One account proposes that the sign was reused because the words sounded alike, but the proposed sound match is unconfirmed.
